name: Mistastin crater
coord_note: Moved off Mistastin Lake onto Horseshoe Island (Mishta-minishtik), the crater's central uplift, at the Canadian Geographical Names Database point for the island; the old point was on the lake surface. CSA and NASA astronauts have trained in geology at this crater (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistastin_crater).
used_for_note: Field geology training site for CSA and NASA astronauts, including the Artemis II crew.

name: Haughton crater, Devon Island
used_for_note: Said to resemble the Mars surface in more ways than any other Earth place and compared with the Moon's Shackleton crater; used for polar field and EVA trials.

name: Lofoten
coord_note: Representative point inside the Lofoten archipelago, on land on Flakstadøya.
used_for_note: ESA astronaut geology training (PANGAEA) scouts Lofoten, where astronauts are expected to recognise anorthosite, a rock abundant in the lunar highlands.

name: Black Point lava flow
used_for_note: Training and systems-testing ground for lunar missions; NASA tested the Lunar Electric Rover there in 2009.

name: Cinder Lake crater field
coord_note: Centre of the USGS drone-survey area of the crater field; the old point was about 5 km east of the field.
used_for_note: Artificial crater field built in the late 1960s to train Apollo astronauts, still used as an analog environment.

name: Meteor Crater
used_for_note: Apollo astronauts trained there in the 1960s; its impact geology resembles lunar and some Martian material.

name: Kilbourne Hole
used_for_note: Maar crater used to train Apollo crews in geology in 1969-1971 and for simulated moonwalks and instrument tests in 2017.

name: Sedan crater
used_for_note: Main stand-in for lunar impact craters in Apollo astronaut training at the Nevada Test Site from 1965.

name: Sudbury
used_for_note: Impact structure used for impact-geology study and cold-condition habitat simulation for Moon and Mars.

name: Ries crater
used_for_note: Apollo 14 and 17 crews had geological field training there in 1970; ESA uses it for the same purpose (PANGAEA: lunar geology and impact cratering).

name: Lanzarote
coord_note: Moved to Timanfaya National Park, the lava-field part of Lanzarote; the old point was in the island's north-east, outside the lava fields.
used_for_note: ESA PANGAEA astronaut field-geology training in volcanic terrain standing in for the Moon and Mars.

name: Mauna Kea
used_for_note: Volcanic terrain where NASA tests technology, with the HI-SEAS habitat nearby for lunar and Martian surface operations.

name: Askja
used_for_note: NASA trained Apollo astronauts there in geology for lunar missions.

name: Etna
used_for_note: Fresh volcanic soils and rocks where ESA and DLR have tested rovers.

name: Teide
used_for_note: Basalt and phonolite terrain similar to rocks on Mars and used for Moon and Mars instrument tests.

name: Yungay, Atacama
coord_note: Moved to the Yungay area used in Atacama Mars-analog studies (lagoons at -24.079, -69.943 in the cited paper; OpenStreetMap places Yungay at -24.0804, -69.9412).
used_for_note: Hyper-arid core used to test life-detection instruments and drills and to study the dry limit of life.

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
coord_note: Representative point at the centre Wikipedia gives for the Dry Valleys region.
used_for_note: Among the coldest and driest Mars-like places, with permafrost and thin brine films; NASA tested an inflatable habitat there.

name: Gypsum Hill, Axel Heiberg
coord_note: The Frontiers in Microbiology 2017 paper gives the Gypsum Hill spring system at 79°25′N, 90°45′W (79.417, -90.75); our point is about 2 km from it.
used_for_note: Perennial cold hypersaline springs flowing through permafrost, a possible surface sign of Martian subsurface brines.

name: Bockfjorden, Svalbard
coord_note: Between the Jotun (79.456, 13.278) and Troll (79.390, 13.440) spring groups, each within about 5 km.
used_for_note: AMASE Mars analog expeditions study the Bockfjord volcanic complex, whose carbonates resemble those in meteorite ALH84001 and Gusev crater; AMASE also tests life-detection instruments there.

name: Rio Tinto
coord_note: Moved to the Riotinto mining area in the river's headwaters, where the acidic red water and the Mars-analog work are; the old point was not on the Río Tinto.
used_for_note: Iron and sulfate minerals such as hematite and jarosite plus extremophile bacteria; also used for EVA training.

name: MDRS, Utah
used_for_note: Mars Society habitat simulator for crew living and operations, with EVA field trials in Mars-like desert.

name: Qaidam (Dalangtan)
coord_note: Moved from the middle of the Qaidam Basin to the centre of the Dalangtan study area the paper gives (38.0–38.67° N, 91.17–92.17° E); the paper gives no single point for the playa.
used_for_note: High hyper-arid plateau with magnesium sulfate salts like Mars's and haloarchaea.

name: Tso Kar
used_for_note: Proposed as an analog for Martian paleolakes.

name: Puga Valley
coord_note: Puga hot springs at 33°13′39.38″N, 78°18′22.98″E at the mouth of the Puga Valley, as given in the EPSC 2024 abstract (Sánchez-García et al.), which calls Puga and Tso Kar potential analogs of early Mars. Moved about 5 km from the old point.
used_for_note: Boron-rich geothermal springs proposed as a prebiotic analog.

name: Kangerlussuaq
used_for_note: Glacial and periglacial landforms, buried ice and polygonal terrain studied as Mars comparisons.

name: Makgadikgadi
coord_note: Representative point at the Wikipedia point for Sua Pan (the Makgadikgadi article's own point, -20.80, 25.33, was not used). The article text also gives 20°59′32″S 25°58′22″E, 27 km south; Sua Pan covers about 24,000 km², so both lie within the pan area. Not checked on a map layer. Confirmed on 15 November: the point lies inside the OpenStreetMap outline of Sua Pan (relation 9479455).
used_for_note: Salt pans (Sua Pan) studied as analogs for Martian playa, hydrated silica (opal) deposits and groundwater-upwelling settings.
used_for_caution: Source check on 15 November: the "life" label has only weak support in the opened source. It was left as first classified because results had already been computed with it.

name: Pavilion Lake
used_for_note: Microbialite lake used to search for signs of life, with underwater reduced-gravity EVA simulation.

name: Laguna de Tirez
used_for_note: Sulfate-rich, hot-spring terrain used for underwater reduced-gravity EVA simulation.

name: Spotted Lake
used_for_note: Magnesium sulfate brine pools with halophilic organisms, an analog for Martian sulfate environments.

name: Salar de Pajonales
used_for_note: Ca-sulfate salar whose domes and polygons are studied as an early-Mars analog; its endolithic microbial communities and gypsum structures are proposed targets for biosignature exploration.

name: Gros Morne
coord_note: Moved to the Tablelands, the exposed mantle rock that makes Gros Morne a Mars analog; the old point was near the park centre, north-east of them.
used_for_note: Glacial valleys and quartzite for Mars, and oceanic crust for the Moon.

name: Laguna de Antofagasta, Puna
coord_note: Replaced the whole-plateau point with the lake the EPSC 2022 abstract gives at -26.111148, -67.407338 (Catamarca) and calls a new high-altitude Mars analogue site. The abstract title says "Laguna de Alumbrera" and the text says "Laguna de Antofagasta"; the coordinates are the same either way. The id is kept for stability.
used_for_note: High-altitude Andean lake mimicking Noachian and Hesperian Mars conditions, a natural laboratory for early Mars.

name: Death Valley
coord_note: Moved to the valley floor near Badwater; the old point was on the western valley side.
used_for_note: Alluvial fans compared with those at Gale crater; the area is a favorite of scientists planning Mars landing sites.

name: Craters of the Moon
coord_note: Moved 5.8 km to the monument's point.
used_for_note: Basaltic lava terrain with lava tubes, used by the NASA BASALT and FINESSE field campaigns for Mars and the Moon.

name: Kilauea Iki
coord_note: Moved 5.6 km to the crater itself; the old point was south-east of it.
used_for_note: Volcanic dust, basalt and volcanic features used for Moon and Mars technology tests.

name: Bletterbach
used_for_note: ESA PANGAEA training site: the gorge's Permian sedimentary rocks are used to teach Martian sedimentary geology and surface processes.

name: CHILL-ICE lava tube
coord_note: About 1.5 km from the Surtshellir–Stefánshellir lava tube system in Hallmundarhraun, the cave reported for the CHILL-ICE analog mission.
used_for_note: Analog mission in an Icelandic lava tube preparing for habitation and human-robot work in lunar and Martian lava tubes.

name: Iowa corn belt
coord_note: Representative point in Iowa farmland (Story County).

name: Beauce
coord_note: Representative point inside the Beauce; matches the article's point, rural land.

name: Pampas
coord_note: Representative point inside the Pampas, rural Buenos Aires province.

name: Central Ukraine
coord_note: Representative farmland point in Kirovohrad Oblast; the earlier point (49.5, 32.0) fell on the Kremenchuk Reservoir.

name: Amazon near Manaus
coord_note: Representative rainforest point north of Manaus; the old point (-3.0, -60.0) was inside the city. Land cover there is evergreen broadleaf forest.

name: Congo Basin
coord_note: Representative point inside the Congo Basin, Tshopo province.

name: Central Borneo
coord_note: Representative point in inland Borneo, Mahakam Ulu regency.

name: Pantanal
coord_note: Representative point inside the Pantanal wetland; seasonally flooded.

name: Flevoland
coord_note: Representative polder farmland point; the old point was on the edge of Lelystad.

name: Ganges plain near Dhaka
coord_note: Representative rural point on the Ganges–Brahmaputra plain in Dhaka Division.

name: Waikato
coord_note: Representative dairy-farm point; the old point was inside Hamilton city.

name: Kampala
coord_note: The city itself, kept as an ordinary urban control.

name: Grand Erg Oriental
coord_note: Representative point at the Wikipedia article's point (30°N, 6°E), 154 km from the old point. Our land cover marks the cell as bare ground; the point sits near the erg's south-western side and the article gives no boundary to check against. Confirmed on 15 November: the point lies inside the OpenStreetMap outline of the erg, in its western part.

name: Thar
coord_note: Representative point inside the Thar Desert (the article's point).

name: Rub' al Khali
coord_note: Representative point inside the Rub' al Khali (the article's point).

name: Simpson Desert
coord_note: Representative point at the Wikipedia article's point, inside the Simpson Desert (roughly 23–27.5°S, 135–138.5°E).

name: Great Victoria Desert
coord_note: Representative point at the Wikipedia article's point, inside the Great Victoria Desert (roughly 28–31°S, 123–133°E).

name: Kalahari
coord_note: Representative point inside the Kalahari (the article's point).

name: Nain anorthosite massif
coord_note: No published point for the Nain Plutonic Suite found; kept about 4 km from Nain, near where its anorthosite is quarried.

name: Manicouagan crater
coord_note: On René-Levasseur Island, the centre of the ring lake (article: 51.397, -68.692).

name: Lut Desert kaluts
coord_note: Moved to the IUGS Geoheritage point for the Lut yardangs (kaluts); the old point was near the salt flats, not the yardang field.

name: Umm Jirsan lava tube, Harrat Khaybar
coord_note: Moved to the cave given by Stewart et al. 2024; the old point was the centre of the Harrat Khaybar lava field.

name: Emi Koussi, Tibesti
coord_note: Summit coordinates; moved 5.7 km.

name: Yakutsk taiga
coord_note: Representative taiga point about 36 km west of Yakutsk; the old point was in the city by the Lena river.

name: Saskatchewan prairie
coord_note: Representative prairie farmland point near Kenaston, outside any town.

name: Central Finland forest
coord_note: Representative forest point in Laukaa; OpenStreetMap tags the area as forest, not lake.

name: West Siberian plain
coord_note: Representative point in Omsk Oblast at the edge of the Great Vasyugan Mire: wet taiga and bog, ordinary for the plain but not dry ground.

name: Lake Salda
coord_note: Wikipedia point for the lake; the Balci et al. 2019 abstract used by NASA gives 37.55°N, 29.68°E.
analog_for: Carbonate lake and deltas like Jezero crater, Mars (NASA Perseverance landing site).
used_for_note: Carbonate deposits and delta features resembling Jezero crater, studied for Mars sample return targets.

name: Dallol hot springs, Danakil
coord_note: Dallol hot-springs sampling site D1 at 14°14′16.69″N, 40°17′52.08″E, from Cavalazzi et al. 2019 (Wikipedia gives the Danakil Depression at 14.24, 40.30). The same paper puts the Dallol volcano at 14°05′28″N, 40°17′58″E, 27 km south; the hot springs were used.
analog_for: Acidic, salty hydrothermal field standing in for past hydrothermal activity on Mars.
used_for_note: Active volcanism with acidic sulfate hydrothermal deposits resembling past hydrothermal activity on Mars.

name: El Tatio geysers
coord_note: Wikipedia point for the geyser field.
analog_for: High, dry, high-UV hot-spring field whose silica deposits resemble those Spirit found at Home Plate, Gusev crater, Mars.
used_for_note: Geysers with high elevation, daily freeze-thaw and intense UV, a closer Mars analog than Yellowstone for life.

name: Arkaroola
coord_note: Wikipedia point for the Arkaroola village area; the Arkaroola Mars Analogue Region covers the wider northern Flinders Ranges.
analog_for: Arid ranges with hot springs and ancient sediments, named the Arkaroola Mars Analogue Region (West et al. 2010).
used_for_note: Assessed as an Australian Mars Analogue Region for its geology.

name: Don Juan Pond, Wright Valley
coord_note: Wikipedia point; Toner et al. 2017 give 77.565°S, 161.174°E (0.2 km away). About 40 km from our McMurdo Dry Valleys point.
analog_for: Calcium-chloride brine pond that stays liquid in the cold, treated as a Mars analog for brines and recurring slope lineae.
used_for_note: Salt-driven CaCl2 brine pond fed by near-surface brine (deliquescence plus some meltwater); studied as an analog for Martian brine flows (RSL) and chloride deposits.
used_for_caution: Source check on 15 November: no opened source supports the "life" label for this site, and "resources" only loosely. The labels were left as first classified because results had already been computed with them.

name: Lava Beds National Monument
coord_note: Wikipedia point for the monument.
analog_for: Lava-tube field where NASA's BRAILLE project rehearses robotic cave exploration for Mars and the Moon.
used_for_note: NASA BRAILLE rehearsed cave-rover exploration in its lava tubes for the Moon and Mars.

name: Stillwater Complex
coord_note: Point from the NASA Earth Observatory article's map link (south of Nye, Montana); Wikipedia gives 45.386, -109.903.
analog_for: Near-pure anorthosite like the lunar highlands, used to make highland dust simulants.
used_for_note: Nearly pure anorthite matching lunar highland anorthosite, used to make lunar highland simulants.

name: Miyake-jima
coord_note: Wikidata point for the island. The island is about 55 km², smaller than one 0.5° grid cell, so a score here is mostly sea. Checked on rock only, not on the overall south-pole score: the island is smaller than one grid cell and its analog value is the anorthite crystals in its lava, which no trait here measures. Set before any v1 scoring run.
analog_for: Island volcano whose anorthite crystals are proposed as an analog for lunar crust rock (Roy et al. 2025, American Mineralogist); a rock analog, not a terrain one.
used_for_note: Natural anorthite studied by infrared spectra as an analog of lunar crustal material.
